Let \(t=\tan\theta\). From
\[
3\sin\theta+\cos\theta=\sqrt{10},
\]
divide by \(\sqrt{10}\):
\[
\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\sin\theta+\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\cos\theta=1.
\]
Thus \(\sin(\theta+\phi)=1\), where \(\tan\phi=\frac13\). Hence
\[
\theta+\phi=\frac{\pi}{2},\quad \tan\theta=\cot\phi=3.
\]

Using the reflection identity:
\[
\tan x-\frac1{\tan x}=-2\cot 2x.
\]
So
\[
\tan\left(\theta+\frac{\pi}{8}\right)-\frac{1}{\tan\left(\theta+\frac{\pi}{8}\right)}
= -2\cot\left(2\theta+\frac{\pi}{4}\right).
\]

Now
\[
\tan 2\theta=\frac{2(3)}{1-3^2}=-\frac34.
\]
Therefore
\[
\tan\left(2\theta+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)
=\frac{-\frac34+1}{1+\frac34}
=\frac17.
\]
So
\[
-2\cot\left(2\theta+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=-2\cdot 7=-14.
\]

\[
\boxed{-14}
\]
